Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

from there adverb

also thence, from over there, from where you are

classical

Cato Agr. 1.2: utī inde exīre possīs
Cic. Att. 12.15.1: nōn exeō inde ante vesperum

inde

adverb

from there (the place named); then

The unemphatic “from there”; it answers unde. Also of time, “then, next” (Cic. Fam. 16.9.2).

Other words

  • illinc — from over there

    adverb · also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 4.7.13: illinc hūc trānsferētur virgō (Lewis & Short); Cic. Att. 9.11.3: quī … illinc profectī erant; Traupman 319; Traupman 360

  • istinc — from there (where you are)

    adverb · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 1.10.1: quī istinc veniunt; Plaut. Capt. 603b: Istinc loquere, sī quid vīs

Examples

  • cumque māne mē in silvam abstrūsī dēnsam et asperam, nōn exeō inde ante vesperum

    and once I have hidden myself in the morning in the thick, wild wood, I don’t come out of it before eveningCic. Att. 12.15.1

  • nōs eō diē cēnātī solvimus; inde austrō lēnissimō caelō serēnō nocte illā et diē posterō in Ītaliam ad Hydrūntem lūdibundī pervēnimus

    we set sail that day after dinner; from there, with a very gentle south wind and a clear sky, we reached Italy at Hydrus that night and the next day, as easily as if at playCic. Fam. 16.9.2

  • inde domum mē ad porrī et ciceris referō laganīque catīnum

    from there I take myself home to a dish of leeks and chickpeas and pancakesHor. S. 1.6.114–115

  • Istinc loquere, sī quid vīs, procul. tamen audiam.

    Speak from there, if you want something; I’ll hear you even at a distance.Plaut. Capt. 603b

See also from here, there, there, where from.
